html:
Kwanlin Dün First Nation is the Indigenous community of the Whitehorse area in southern Yukon. Its people are mostly of Southern Tutchone and Tagish descent, with Tlingit ties. Kwanlin means "water running through a canyon", for Miles Canyon on the Yukon River.

The canyon and the White Horse Rapids below it were a fishing place for salmon. In 1898 the Klondike Gold Rush put the site on the route north, and the White Pass railway reached Whitehorse in 1900. The town grew over their camps, and the Kwanlin Dün were moved several times. They signed a land claim and self-government agreement in 2005. See also Carcross/Tagish and Tlingit.
